target_audience.primary_persona: Professional software developers who want to accelerate their development workflow by delegating coding tasks to autonomous AI agents
secondary_personas: Solo developers and indie hackers who need to multiply their productivity
Development teams looking for autonomous QA and code generation
Open-source maintainers who want AI assistance with issues and PRs
pain_points: Spending too much time on repetitive coding tasks
AI tools require constant supervision and manual intervention
Fear of AI making changes directly to main branch without safety
Losing context between coding sessions with AI assistants
Managing complex multi-file refactoring is tedious
Limited productivity gains from single-agent AI tools
goals: Delegate entire coding tasks and focus on higher-level work
Build features faster without sacrificing code quality
Run multiple tasks in parallel to maximize throughput
Have AI remember project context across sessions
Safely experiment with AI-generated code in isolation
target_audience.usage_context: Desktop application used during active development sessions. Developers describe tasks in natural language, and autonomous agents plan, implement, test, and prepare code for merge while the developer focuses on other work or reviews.

product_vision.one_liner: Autonomous multi-agent coding framework that plans, builds, and validates software for you
product_vision.problem_statement: Existing AI coding tools require constant human supervision, operate on single files, lack persistent memory, and provide no safety mechanisms - making true delegation of coding tasks impossible
product_vision.value_proposition: Turret is the open-source autonomous coding alternative that lets developers truly delegate entire tasks. It plans, implements across multiple files, validates through QA, and safely isolates changes in git worktrees - all while retaining context across sessions through its Memory Layer.
success_metrics: Number of tasks completed autonomously without human intervention
Time saved per developer using Turret vs manual coding
Active installations and daily active users
Merge success rate (tasks that pass QA and merge cleanly)

existing_features: Autonomous task execution with planning, implementation, and validation
Parallel execution with up to 12 agent terminals
Git worktree isolation for safe development
Self-validating QA loop before code reaches user
Memory Layer for cross-session context retention
Kanban board for visual task management
Agent terminals with one-click task context injection
Ideation for discovering improvements and vulnerabilities
CLI mode for headless operation and CI/CD integration
Linear integration for project management sync
known_gaps: Advanced merge completion recording not yet implemented (workspace.py line 141)
Advanced conflict analysis checks are placeholder TODOs
Email alerts for health monitoring not implemented
technical_debt: Some route detection examples in analyzers may need real implementation
Password hashing placeholder in test output validator
Health monitor email alerts marked as TODO

alternatives: Cursor - AI-powered code editor with inline suggestions
GitHub Copilot - AI pair programming assistant
Claude Code CLI - Anthropic's official CLI tool
differentiators: Open-source alternative to Devin with full autonomy - accessible to all developers
Memory Layer providing cross-session context that no competitor offers
Multi-agent parallel execution unique to Turret (up to 12 agents)
Git worktree isolation for safe autonomous development
Self-validating QA loop before any code reaches main branch
Desktop-native experience with Kanban board vs terminal-only tools
competitive_context.market_position: Open-source autonomous AI coding framework positioned as the accessible alternative to Devin. Turret uniquely combines full autonomy, multi-agent parallel execution, persistent memory, and git worktree safety - capabilities that no other open-source tool provides together. This addresses the large gap between expensive closed-source solutions (Devin) and limited suggestion-based tools (Copilot, Cursor).
competitor_pain_points: All non-Devin competitors require constant human supervision and cannot work autonomously
No competitor offers persistent cross-session memory for project context
No competitor provides built-in QA validation before code reaches user
Most tools work in single-agent mode with no parallel execution capabilities
IDE-based tools lack safety mechanisms when AI modifies code directly
Devin is the only autonomous alternative but is closed-source and expensive

technical: Requires Claude Pro/Max subscription for API access
Python 3.12+ required for backend and Memory Layer
Native dependencies (real_ladybug) require C++ compiler on some systems
Git must be initialized in target projects
dependencies: Anthropic Claude API for agent intelligence
GitHub Actions for CI/CD and releases
